perspective:
Vincent Chinana’s available information:

- Vincent knows himself as a mechanic. He knows Patrick Guzman as a long-time friend, a construction worker, and someone he has known since their teenage years; they share a blue-collar bond and have collaborated on projects using Vincent’s mechanical skills and Patrick’s construction expertise.
- At a local diner, Vincent asks Patrick about a new construction venture. He hears Patrick say it seems like a good opportunity to expand his business. Vincent says he has heard it is risky, asks if Patrick is sure, and expresses worry that it could jeopardize financial security, suggesting Patrick reconsider or delay until he has more information. Patrick says he appreciates the concern and will think it over more.
- After a few days, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussions about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent says they need to talk and that he feels Patrick is not telling him everything. Patrick says it is complicated and he did not want to worry Vincent with details. Vincent says that is exactly why they need to discuss it, that he is Patrick’s friend, and that he feels betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick apologizes, says he should have been more open, and agrees to sit down and explain everything.
- During a detailed discussion at Vincent’s garage, Vincent learns the investment situation is serious. Patrick tells him it has been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanks him and says he is grateful for the support.
- A month later, at a coffee shop, Vincent has information suggesting the venture might actually turn a profit. He tells Patrick this. Patrick says it is starting to look up and that he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting him earlier and proposes a joint venture, saying he now sees a lot of potential. Patrick agrees and says they should work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick are optimistic about their joint venture. Vincent says that combining their skills can make it a success and that they should start drafting a business plan, outlining every step carefully. Patrick agrees, says he is excited, and agrees they should cover all bases and set it up for success.
- Vincent’s own actions include: meeting Patrick at the diner, construction site, coffee shop, his garage, and his house; raising concerns about the investment; noticing Patrick’s avoidance; confronting Patrick about transparency; offering a loan; apologizing for doubting him; proposing a joint venture; and beginning to draft a business plan.

Vincent does not have access to Patrick’s private thoughts, hidden events, or information Patrick did not tell him or show him.
